fixes.explanation: Verse 16 says Paul was in a hurry to reach Jerusalem, if possible, by the day of Pentecost. That's why he decided to sail past Ephesus. He didn't want to spend time in the province of Asia. I'd say that's a man watching the calendar, friend.
Paul says he taught them publicly and from house to house. That covers the big gatherings and the living rooms. He also says he did not shrink back from declaring anything that was helpful to them.

I bet Paul cares about these elders, but that's not what he names here. He says he wants to finish his course and complete the ministry he received from the Lord Jesus. In fact, a few verses later he tells them they won't see his face again (Acts 20:25).

Paul says he's going to Jerusalem not knowing what will happen to him there. He only knows that chains and afflictions await him. What matters to him is finishing his course and completing the ministry he received from the Lord Jesus.
Paul doesn't say they'll just walk away. He says men will rise up and distort the truth to draw away disciples after them. The danger he names is twisted teaching, not quiet leaving.
That's close to the story, but it isn't the word. Paul says his own hands ministered to his needs and those of his companions. The work he points to is the work of his hands.
No tears held back here, friend. The text says, “They all wept openly as they embraced Paul and kissed him.” They wept openly, right there in front of everybody.
Verse 38 says they accompanied him to the ship. They'd prayed and wept together, and they still went with him there. I think nobody wanted to be the first to turn around.
Jerusalem is where Paul is headed, but that's not where the text says the elders go. It says they accompanied him to the ship. That's the place the passage names.
